chunks.title: Grounding and Electric Shock Prevention
chunks.content: This appliance must be grounded via a permanent wiring system or equipment grounding conductor; improper grounding can result in electric shock. Check with a qualified electrician if in doubt.

scenarios.condition: Uncertain if appliance is properly grounded
steps: Check with a qualified electrician or authorized service representative.
Do not connect the appliance if it has been damaged in transit.
Do not attempt to bypass grounding wire yourself.

chunks.title: Hydrogen Gas Risk from Unused Hot Water System
chunks.content: Hydrogen gas can accumulate and become explosive if a hot water system connected to the dishwasher has been unused for two weeks or more; run all hot water faucets for several minutes before use and do not smoke or use open flame.

scenarios.condition: Hot water system unused for two weeks or longer
steps: Turn on all hot water faucets and let water flow from each for several minutes.
Do not smoke or use an open flame during this process.
Then proceed to use the dishwasher normally.

chunks.title: Safe Loading and Sharp Item Handling
chunks.content: Load knives and sharp utensils with handles up (or points/edges down per basket instructions) to reduce cut injuries, and locate sharp items so they don't damage the door seal.

chunks.title: Hot Water and Steam on Door Opening
chunks.content: Hot water or steam may escape when opening the door during or after a cycle; wait until water noises stop and steam subsides before fully opening the door.

chunks.title: Avoid Harsh Chemicals and Steam Cleaners
chunks.content: Do not use bleach-based products or steam/high-pressure cleaners on the dishwasher, as these can damage the appliance and present health hazards.

chunks.title: Risk to Children
chunks.content: Do not allow children to play in or on the dishwasher; remove the door of an old dishwasher before discarding to prevent entrapment.

chunks.title: Familiarizing with Appliance Components
chunks.content: Key components include the detergent dispenser, upper/lower racks, spray arms, filter system, silverware basket/drawer, rinse aid dispenser, and rating plate located inside the door.

chunks.title: Control Panel Overview
chunks.content: The control panel includes ON/OFF, cycle buttons, rinse aid indicator, water supply display, wireless network display, options buttons, start button, remote start, and main display for basic settings.

chunks.title: Dishwasher Cycles Overview
chunks.content: Cycles include Pots & Pans, Auto, Normal, Hand Wash, Quick, and Favorite, each with different temperatures, durations, and consumption values.

chunks.title: Energy Guide and Favorite Cycle
chunks.content: The Energy Guide rating is based on the Normal soil-sensing cycle without rinse aid; the Favorite function lets you save a Cycle and Option combination via the app or on the appliance control panel.

chunks.title: Options Overview
chunks.content: Available options include Extra Dry (raises final rinse temp for better drying), Power Boost (increases spray pressure for mixed soil loads), and Sanitize (raises temperature/cycle length for sanitizing items like cutting boards and baby bottles).

chunks.title: Adjusting Upper Rack Height
chunks.content: Pull out the upper rack, hold it steady, press the side levers, raise or lower it evenly, release levers to click into position, then slide the rack back in.

chunks.title: Cup Shelf, Flip Tines, and Silverware Basket Use
chunks.content: The cup shelf holds small cups/glasses or large utensils and can be folded up; flip tines can be folded down to fit pans, bowls, and glasses; the silverware basket holds silverware with sharp points down.

chunks.title: Rack Height Settings Table
chunks.content: Rack height settings vary by whether the appliance uses a silverware basket or silverware drawer, with three adjustable positions for upper and lower rack diameters.

chunks.title: Initial Use Setup Steps
chunks.content: Before first use: add rinse aid, add detergent (using correct amount per dispenser markings), turn on the appliance, set the rinse aid amount, then run the highest-temperature cycle empty to clear manufacturing residues.

chunks.title: Rinse Aid System: Adding, Setting Amount, and Switching Off
chunks.content: Open the rinse aid dispenser lid, fill to the max mark, and close; adjust the dispensed amount via basic settings (r:00-r:06) if streaking or spotting occurs; can be switched off entirely if using a combination detergent.

chunks.title: Dishware Compatibility and Damage Prevention
chunks.content: Only wash dishwasher-safe items; avoid wooden utensils, antique/decorative glassware, non-heat-resistant plastics, copper/tin dishes, and items soiled with ash, wax, grease, or paint to prevent damage.

chunks.title: Loading Dishware Correctly
chunks.content: Remove large food remnants (do not pre-rinse), place heavily soiled items in the lower rack, arrange dishware stably with openings facing down, keep spray arms unobstructed, and load silverware points/edges down.

chunks.title: Removing Dishware Safely
chunks.content: Allow dishes to cool a few minutes with door slightly open after the cycle ends, then unload starting from the bottom rack upward to prevent water dripping onto lower items.

chunks.title: Basic Operation: Starting, Interrupting, and Terminating a Cycle
chunks.content: Touch ON/OFF briefly to power on, press Start to begin the cycle; to interrupt press On/Off then press Start to resume; to terminate early, open door, hold Reset ~4 seconds, close door, and wait ~1 minute for cancellation.

chunks.content: Basic settings include rinse aid dispensing level, sensor setting, Extra Dry, infoLight, start cycle default, signal/button volume, Wi-Fi, Remote Start, and factory reset, each with a display code and selectable range.

chunks.title: Home Connect App Setup
chunks.content: Install the Home Connect app on a mobile device, follow in-app registration steps, ensure appliance receives Wi-Fi signal and the door is closed, then scan the provided QR code to link the appliance.

chunks.title: Filter System Cleaning
chunks.content: Check filters for food residue after each dishwashing cycle and clean per the manufacturer's video (accessible via QR code) to maintain wash performance.

chunks.title: Spray Arm Cleaning
chunks.content: If dishware is not washed properly, clean the upper and lower spray arms; instructions are provided via QR code link.

chunks.title: Water Supply and Sensor Error Codes
chunks.content: Error codes E:20-60 through E:34-00 indicate issues like calcified heating element, activated water protection system, closed/jammed water valve, kinked inlet hose, or continuous water inflow.

chunks.content: Codes E:61-02/03 indicate drain pump cover or blockage issues (not a true fault); E:90-01 signals low power voltage; E:92-40 signals soiled/blocked filters; all-LED flashing may indicate a software update or electronics fault requiring reset.

chunks.title: Food Remnants, Streaks, and Rust on Dishware
chunks.content: Food remnants left on dishes can result from overcrowding, blocked spray arms/filters, or a too-light cycle; streaks on glassware are usually from rinse aid dosage or precleaning; rust on silverware indicates insufficiently rust-resistant items or contact with rusting items.

chunks.title: Detergent Residue and Sanitize Display
chunks.content: Detergent residue in the dispenser or collecting tray is usually caused by blocked spray arms or a damp dispenser at fill time; a 'SAnl' display simply indicates the Sanitize option completed and is not an error.

chunks.title: Clean the Drain Pump Procedure
chunks.content: Disconnect power, remove racks and filter system, scoop out water, pry off the pump cover with a spoon, remove debris around the impeller by hand, then reinstall the cover, filter, and racks.

chunks.title: Transporting the Appliance
chunks.content: Empty the appliance, secure loose parts, run the highest-temperature cycle briefly then terminate it after ~4 minutes to drain, switch off, close the water valve, and detach the supply hose to drain residual water; always transport upright.

chunks.title: Vacation and Winterizing Preparation
chunks.content: Before vacation in warm weather, shut off water supply near the dishwasher in addition to the main valve; in cold weather or for extended non-use in freezing conditions, have the dishwasher winterized by a professional service.

chunks.title: Old Appliance Disposal Safety
chunks.content: Unplug the appliance, cut the power cord, and remove the door before disposal to avoid entrapment risk; check local recycling programs for large appliances.

chunks.title: Technical Specifications
chunks.content: Max weight 60 kg/132 lbs; 120V 60Hz, 1440W, 12A fuse; water pressure 7.25-145 psi; min inlet rate 2.6 gal/min; hot water max 140°F; load capacity 16 place settings.

chunks.title: Customer Service Contact Info
chunks.content: Contact Thermador Customer Service in USA/Canada at 1-800-735-4328 or via thermador.com/support; have the model number (E-Nr.), production number (FD), and consecutive numbering (Z-Nr.) from the rating plate ready.

tasks.title: Clean the Filter System
tasks.description: Check and clean the dishwasher's filter system to remove trapped food residue.
tasks.justification: Clogged filters cause poor wash results, drainage problems, and unpleasant odors.
tasks.instructions_text: After each wash cycle, check the filter for food residue. Remove the filter assembly, rinse it under water to clear debris, and reinsert it securely (see QR-linked video for detailed steps).

tasks.title: Clean the Spray Arms
tasks.description: Remove and clean the upper and lower spray arm nozzles when dishes aren't washing properly.
tasks.justification: Blocked spray arm nozzles reduce water pressure and cause food remnants to remain on dishware.
tasks.instructions_text: Remove the upper and lower spray arms, rinse the nozzles under running water to clear blockages, and check that they rotate freely before reinstalling (see QR-linked video for detailed steps).

tasks.title: Clean the Drain Pump
tasks.description: Inspect and clear the drain pump of food remnants or foreign objects when water isn't draining properly.
tasks.justification: A blocked drain pump prevents water from draining, leaving standing water and poor wash results.
tasks.instructions_text: Disconnect power, remove the racks and filter system, scoop out any standing water, pry off the pump cover with a spoon, and remove debris from around the impeller by hand. Reinstall the cover, filter, and racks afterward.

tasks.title: Descale the Heating Element
tasks.description: Descale the dishwasher when the display shows a calcified heating element error code.
tasks.justification: Calcium scale buildup on the heating element reduces heating efficiency and can trigger error codes or premature failure.
tasks.instructions_text: When error E:20-60 appears, run a dishwasher descaling product through a cycle, then operate the appliance using the water softening system if equipped.

tasks.title: Add Rinse Aid to Dispenser
tasks.description: Refill the rinse aid dispenser when the refill indicator lights up.
tasks.justification: Skipping rinse aid refills leads to water spots, streaking, and poor drying results.
tasks.instructions_text: Press the catch on the rinse aid dispenser lid and lift it open, fill with rinse aid up to the max mark, wipe up any spills in the tub, then close the lid until it clicks.

tasks.title: Winterize the Dishwasher
tasks.description: Have the dishwasher professionally winterized before extended non-use in freezing conditions.
tasks.justification: Freezing water inside the appliance can damage the fill valve and internal components, and freeze damage is not covered under warranty.
tasks.instructions_text: Before leaving the dishwasher unused in a location that will experience freezing temperatures, arrange for a professional service to winterize the unit.

tasks.title: Shut Off Water Before Vacation
tasks.description: Turn off the water supply near the dishwasher before leaving for an extended vacation.
tasks.justification: Leaving the water supply on during an extended absence increases the risk of undetected leaks causing water damage.
tasks.instructions_text: Before leaving for vacation during warmer weather, turn off the water supply at the shutoff valve nearest the dishwasher in addition to the main water valve.

tasks.title: Secure Drain Pump Cover
tasks.description: Verify the drain pump cover is properly seated and clicked into place if error code E:61-02 appears.
tasks.justification: A loose drain pump cover or foreign object blocking the pump prevents proper drainage.
tasks.instructions_text: If error E:61-02 appears, open the pump area, check for foreign objects blocking the impeller, remove them, and press the pump cover down until it clicks securely into place.

tasks.title: Verify Grounding Connection
tasks.description: Confirm the dishwasher is properly connected to a grounded electrical supply at installation.
tasks.justification: Improper grounding increases risk of electric shock in the event of a malfunction.
tasks.instructions_text: At installation, have a qualified electrician verify the appliance is connected to a properly grounded metal permanent wiring system or equipment grounding conductor.

re_check_triggers.description: Burning smell, sparks, or shock felt when touching the appliance

tasks.title: Flush Hot Water Line Before First Use
tasks.description: Run hot water faucets to clear accumulated hydrogen gas if the hot water system has been unused for two weeks or more, prior to connecting/using the dishwasher.
tasks.justification: Accumulated hydrogen gas in an unused hot water system is explosive if not released before appliance use.
tasks.instructions_text: Before connecting or using a dishwasher on a hot water system unused for two weeks or more, turn on all hot water faucets in the home and let water run from each for several minutes.

re_check_triggers.description: Gas-like odor noticed near hot water fixtures after extended non-use

tasks.title: Run Initial Empty Cleaning Cycle
tasks.description: Run the highest-temperature cycle without dishware the first time the appliance is used.
tasks.justification: Running an empty cycle at first use clears manufacturing residues and marks before washing real dishware.
tasks.instructions_text: After adding rinse aid and detergent and turning on the appliance for the first time, select the cycle with the highest cleaning temperature and run it empty (no dishware) to remove manufacturing residues.

weekly.title: Weekly / Routine Care
steps: Check the filter system for food residue after each wash cycle and rinse it clean.
Check that spray arm nozzles are unobstructed and can rotate freely.
Wipe up any spilled rinse aid or detergent from the tub to prevent frothing.
Refill the rinse aid dispenser when the refill indicator lights up.

deep_clean.title: Periodic Deep Clean
steps: Remove and clean the filter system thoroughly.
Remove the upper and lower spray arms and clean out the nozzles.
Disconnect power and clean the drain pump of debris or foreign objects.
Run a descaling product through a cycle if scale buildup is detected (error E:20-60).
Check the door seal and tub for soiling and clean if necessary.
